preamble: Araucaria's first puzzle (then still anonymous) appeared in the Manchester Guardian 50 years ago today.

clue.text: 12 19 (here) to treat last cause of AIDS in the past

parts.note: to doctor a patient is to treat them medically
Z is the last letter of the alphabet
HIV is the virus that causes AIDS
ago means in the past, as in 'long ago'

explanation.surface: A doctor treating the final victims of an epidemic in years gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: '12 19' sends you to FIFTY-YEAR-OLD; Pasternak's novel reached British readers in 1958, fifty years before this puzzle, hence '(here)'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasternak's novel came out in Britain in 1958, so at the time of this anniversary puzzle it was half a century old.

clue.text: Sweet work, half in the open: turn to it (

taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The clue as held ends on a stray bracket; the parse needs only the words before it. Opal Fruits were British chewy sweets, now sold as Starburst.
explanation.definitionFit: Opal Fruits were a brand of fruit-flavoured chewy confectionery, so the brand is an example of a sweet.

definitions.meaning: naff is British slang for cheap, vulgar or in poor taste
sticky, as wet paint or glue still is

explanation.definitionFit: Tacky covers both senses: tasteless and cheap-looking, and slightly sticky to the touch.

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
red is the colour of the political left
os is the Latin and anatomical word for bone

explanation.surface: Military engineers leave a bone lying behind the church altar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a direction or a verb, but it is the politics of the left, RED.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is the ornamental screen or panel standing at the back of a church altar, so it sits behind it.

clue.text: Leader for clique giving private audience

parts.note: a head is a leader, as of a school or department
a set is a clique or exclusive social group

explanation.surface: The head of an exclusive circle grants someone a private meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private audience' suggests an interview with a dignitary; here it is listening on your own through earphones.
explanation.definitionFit: Headphones let one wearer listen privately, so the device gives its user a private hearing.

clue.text: 12 19 success circum-navigating ocean: it is flawed

indicators.note: circumnavigating means sailing right round, so the synonym for success goes around the other letters

parts.note: victory means success or triumph

indicators.note: flawed means imperfect or broken, so the preceding letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A triumphant round-the-world voyage that turns out to have its faults.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon makes 'ocean: it is flawed' read as a comment on the voyage, but 'flawed' is the anagram signal. The Victorian Society, which campaigns for nineteenth-century buildings, was founded in 1958.
explanation.definitionFit: The conservation group was set up in 1958, so it was turning fifty when this anniversary puzzle appeared.

parts.note: a rave is a lively party or shindig

explanation.surface: Asking whether a lively party is genuinely good fun.
explanation.walkthrough: Grave is a musical tempo marking, telling the player to perform slowly and seriously, so it can stand for an adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: As a direction in a musical score the Italian marking means play solemnly, that is, in a serious manner.

clue.text: 12 19 (coining a phrase) 20th of a dime and a run I made

parts.note: a dime is ten cents, so a twentieth of it is half a cent

indicators.note: made signals that the letters are formed into something new, an anagram

explanation.surface: A coin collector boasting about a tiny coin and a run of good luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges A RUN I into URIAN. The answer is a coined word, hence '(coining a phrase)', and the coin theme runs through the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aged fifty has lived half a century, so the invented term describes a person reaching that age.

parts.note: the Wests, Timothy and his son Samuel, are a British acting family
the ides is a date in the Roman calendar, the 15th or 13th of the month
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A theatrical family arranges a date with a Conservative politician.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical opened on Broadway in 1957 and in London in 1958, hence '(here)': fifty years old in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical premiered in London in 1958, so by this anniversary puzzle the British production was half a century old.

clue.text: 12 19, a right old way of dating a number

parts.note: AUC, ab urbe condita, dated Roman years from the founding of the city
an aria is a musical number, a song in an opera

explanation.surface: An antiquated method of assigning dates to a numbered sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter clues his own pseudonym; his first Guardian puzzle appeared fifty years before this one.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter's first puzzle appeared in 1958, so by this anniversary he had been setting for half a century.

parts.note: tee said out loud sounds like tea, and cha is a word for tea
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A golfer told to use a rubber tee along with an iron club.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf picture of tee and iron hides tea (CHA) and the element. 'Use rubber' means act as something that rubs.
explanation.definitionFit: To chafe is to rub or abrade, which is what something used as a rubber does.

clue.text: Variant of "Tie a dry fly" first appearing in 1958

indicators.note: a variant is a different version, so the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fishing-fly pattern, a version of an older one, first tied in 1958.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variant of' looks like an indicator with a link, but OF is part of the twelve letters rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything that first appeared in 1958 had reached half a century by 2008, when this puzzle ran.

parts.note: a dish is a plate
taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A plate bent in one direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' looks like a description of the plate, but it is the definition: bent as in crooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Bent is slang for corrupt or crooked, describing someone who cheats or deceives.

parts.note: requites means repays or returns a favour or injury

explanation.surface: Horsemen of Rome come back without their commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaderless' drops the R from REQUITES. 'Returns' reads as a noun but is the verb repays.
explanation.definitionFit: The equites were the equestrian order of ancient Rome, the class known as knights.

indicators.note: a total disaster means everything is wrecked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nobleman wrecking proceedings in an utter fiasco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disaster' rearranges DUKE and TOTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill that is filibustered is defeated by speaking until the time runs out, which is the idiom used.

parts.note: a trip is a journey
O is round in shape
12 is FIFTY, which is L in Roman numerals
one is I in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A journey around the city.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference 12 gives the word fifty, and with 1 it becomes the Roman numerals L and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital city of Libya.

clue.text: The exception, not even an island, eliminated

parts.note: odd numbers are not even
the Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea
out means knocked out or eliminated

explanation.surface: A peculiar island is wiped off the list.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is a self-governing island between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The odd one out is the item that differs from the rest of a group, the one exception.

parts.note: taken as written
to tally is to agree or correspond

explanation.surface: Every single one comes round to agreeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes' is a link word; 'comes to' wants to be a sum, but TO stands as itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Totally means completely, with nothing left out, so it fits without exception.

clue.text: Do wrong drug and snuff it, who knows when?

parts.note: to sin is to do wrong
E is ecstasy, the drug
to snuff it is slang for to die

explanation.surface: Misbehave, take drugs and die, and who can say when it will happen?
explanation.walkthrough: Sine die is Latin for without a day: an adjournment with no date set.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjournment sine die has no fixed date for resuming, so nobody knows when it will happen.

clue.text: To judge by his law, a Roman has a way to conduct impulses

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, judges a match
lex is Latin for law, the Roman's own word
RC stands for Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: Judging by the laws of Rome, a citizen finds a way to manage his urges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a Roman' looks like a citizen of Rome; it is A plus RC, Roman Catholic.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflex arc is the nerve pathway that carries the signal for a reflex action, a route for nerve impulses.

indicators.note: sound signals that the words for the jolly chap are said out loud

parts.note: a jolly chap is a fun guy

explanation.surface: A cheerful man, sound in mind, sitting on toadstools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like healthy; it is the instruction to say 'fun guy' out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Toadstools are a kind of mushroom-like fruiting body, members of the kingdom of moulds and mushrooms.

definitions.meaning: Ulysses S. ... was a US general and president, so his surname is Ulysses'
a ... is a sum allowed or awarded, such as a student ...

explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the American general Ulysses S. Grant, and also a sum of money awarded or allowed.

clue.text: Escaping from the deluge, Noah reached port

explanation.surface: Fleeing the Flood, Noah's Ark finally reached harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Escaping from' pulls the run out across 'deluGE NOAh'.
explanation.definitionFit: Genoa is a major Italian seaport on the Ligurian coast.

clue.text: Any odd house not quite in Northants and not quite in Oxon

definitions.text: not quite in Northants and not quite in Oxon

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A curious house that sits on the border between two English counties.
explanation.walkthrough: Aynho is a village in Northamptonshire right on the Oxfordshire border, so it is only just in one county and only just out of the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The village lies at the very edge of Northamptonshire, beside Oxfordshire, so it sits barely on one side of the county line.

definitions.meaning: Pinter's play premiered in 1958, so it was turning fifty
a celebration suited to the setter's anniversary today
